summary: The change adds [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to every type emitted by the MessagePack source generator (formatters, resolvers, enum and union formatters, composite resolvers), guarded by #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK so netstandard2.0/.NET Framework consumers still compile. All six T4 templates and their checked-in generated outputs emit the attribute; the two new tests pass on head and fail on base source, and the full 169-test generator suite passes on head. One unrelated formatting change in TransformUtilities.cs is out of scope.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: All six source-generator templates emit [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] behind the #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK guard (e.g. ResolverTemplate.tt lines 14-16 and FormatterTemplate.tt lines 14-16; the same pattern appears in CompositeResolverTemplate, EnumTemplate, StringKeyFormatterTemplate and UnionTemplate), the checked-in generated outputs were regenerated accordingly, the new test CodeCoverageExclusionTests.AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage passes on head and failed on base source, and the full 169-test generator suite passes on head.

evidence.quote: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

findings.title: Unrelated formatting change in TransformUtilities.cs outside the requirement scope
findings.claim: TransformUtilities.cs line 58 changed the brace emission for nested types that carry type constraints from emitting just "{" to emitting "{\r\n", adding a newline after the opening brace in generated code. This is unrelated to REQ-2297-F1 (ExcludeFromCodeCoverage) and changes generated output beyond the requirement's scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Revert TransformUtilities.cs to the base line, or move this formatting change to a separate change so this change stays limited to ExcludeFromCodeCoverage emission.

refusals.topic: netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework compilation of generated output
refusals.reason: build.net472/netstandard was not run (Linux container, only net8.0 built), so the #if guard's effect for those targets was not compile-verified; only the template text was inspected.
refusals.who_should_decide: area owner / maintainer with a multi-target build

refusals.reason: tests.execution was not run: SDK 8.0.402 ships Roslyn 4.11 while the generator references Microsoft.CodeAnalysis 4.12.0, so execution test projects fail to compile (CS9057/CS0117); this mismatch exists on base too and is environmental, not caused by the change.
